A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same REvolve study, with readable main text, references, and Appendices A–G. Full-document text and rendering comparisons establish that changes are confined to the first-page version stamp and Figure 3 with its surrounding layout.

before.justification: v3 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments on autonomous driving, humanoid locomotion, and Adroit Hand manipulation, human-preference evaluations in Table 2, and supplementary experimental results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation and human-preference results and displays additional generations in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the evolutionary procedure in Section 3, and the appendix prompts and reward code are unchanged. Both versions use the same GPT-4 reward generation, genetic operators, and human-feedback mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three tasks and the same two additional AirSim generalization environments. Extending Figure 3 across more generations adds no task or environment coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains REvolve, REvolve Auto, Eureka, Eureka Auto, and Expert Designed, with Human Driving additionally shown for autonomous driving. Comparator membership in Tables 2–3 and the appendix experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 already specifies N = 7 generations and K = 16 individuals in both versions; training steps, metrics, and evaluation procedures are also unchanged. Figure 3's extension through generation 7 does not establish an increased training budget.

E4.justification: The genetic-operator ablation in Figure 4, generalization evaluations in Table 3 and Figure 13, and supplementary training analysis in Figure 12 are identical. The Figure 3 update extends the existing main comparison without introducing a separate supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report two random seeds in Section 5.2 and Figure 3 and retain the same shaded-band presentation and Table 3 mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. No run-count or statistical estimation practice changes are documented.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds fitness points for generations 6 and 7 for the four learned-reward variants across all three tasks. These show largely plateauing performance while retaining the method ordering. The tables and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward-design formalization and Equation 1, the Elo and fitness definitions in Appendix B, and the reward formulas in Appendix C are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about evolutionary reward search, incorporating human feedback without training an additional reward model, and outperforming the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 already states that improvements diminish and converge by generation 5; v4 retains that interpretation. Explanations of feedback benefits, generalization failures, computational costs, and reliance on closed-source GPT-4 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Training hardware and budgets, RL hyperparameters, fitness calculations, prompts, feedback examples, generated reward code, and code-access statements remain identical in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The citations, bibliography, Section 4, and Appendix D are unchanged, including positioning relative to Eureka, Text2Reward, RLHF, and evolutionary algorithms using LLMs.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 6 April 2025 to v4 dated 23 May 2025. Manuscript prose, headings, captions, and section and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with the generation axis extended from 5 to 7, adjusted tick spacing, and slightly changed panel dimensions and surrounding spacing. Its caption and legends remain unchanged; all other figures and tables retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 now displays results through the generation-7 horizon already specified in Section 5.2, making the late plateau supporting Section 5.4's convergence claim visible. This modestly improves evidential completeness; the methods, other analyses, and main conclusions remain unchanged.
